minutes.headline: Water district voters approved the annual budget, borrowing authority, a $50,000 water repair and a vehicle; Burch won re-election.
minutes.summary: The annual Lunenburg Water District meeting took up six articles. Reports, the operating budget, borrowing in anticipation of revenue, two $50,000 appropriations and the vehicle purchase were approved by voice vote, and Article One was postponed until the ballot count. The meeting recessed for the count and then announced the election results and adjourned.

what_happened.line: Voters approved the operating and maintenance budget for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2024, and fixed officers' salaries, by voice vote.
Voters unanimously authorized the treasurer to borrow in anticipation of revenue and renew notes; no dollar cap was stated, only what is needed to fund the budget.
Voters unanimously approved two further appropriations: one from the water enhancement account for repair of water services, one from surplus revenue for a replacement vehicle.
Article One, the election, was postponed until the ballots were counted; after a recess the results were announced, with Mark Burch winning, and the meeting adjourned.

why_it_matters: Water district customers pay for the operating budget through district income, so the Article Three vote sets the spending behind the district's rates for the year starting July 1, 2024.
Short-term borrowing was authorized with no stated limit, so the size of any notes depends on cash needs during the year rather than on a figure voters approved.
